lines: Every morning, for eleven years, someone left a loaf of bread outside room nine.
The old man who lived there, Lucius, never found out who.
Downstairs, Marcus the baker lit his oven before the sun came up.
And before he sold a single loaf, he always set one aside.
He climbed the stairs in the dark, so softly the old wood barely creaked.
He left the bread, and he was gone before anyone woke.
Lucius had no family left. No money to spare.
Just one warm loaf, every single morning. Like a promise someone was keeping.
What Lucius had long forgotten was a winter, forty years before.
A starving boy grabbed a loaf from this very counter, and the baker caught him by the arm.
A stranger stepped in. He paid for the bread, and said: Eat, son. Come back tomorrow. I'll pay for that one too.
One morning, Lucius woke early, and followed the footsteps down the stairs.
The baker only smiled. You fed a hungry boy once, he said. I've just been paying you back.
Sometimes, it just takes forty years to find its way home.
